text:
Baltimore has a new quarterback, Jacoby Brissett, and he says he is on a "crash course" for Monday's game against the Chargers, with no interest in the club's plans for the rest of the season. That's the most sensible thing anyone in purple has said in a month. The odd part is that the line has moved Baltimore's way, from 2.5 points to 4.5. Meanwhile the Ravens' title odds have drifted from 125-1 to 150-1. My read is that the bookies believe in Monday and nothing after it, and so do I. A 4-5 team still learning its quarterback in November, with Rashod Bateman questionable, is filling out a schedule. Rob and Darren hold the Ravens in four bets between them, at 13 to 17 percent apiece. Baltimore wears all-black this week, which seems right for a funeral.

Andy's Lions head to Munich lighter again. Centre Cade Mays is out, and Kerby Joseph and D.J. Reed are now officially out too. Andy is still 83 percent against Darren, but that says more about the Ravens than the Lions.

Darren's real lifeline is Sunday night. His Bengals host Aaron Rodgers' Steelers for the AFC North lead, both at 6-2, despite putting three players on injured reserve this week. Burrow is in the MVP conversation and I'm backing him. Rob, that's your 43 percent with Kansas City burning. Steve holds the Chiefs at 87 percent against both Ravens owners, and nobody else is close.

Andy has spent half a season looking like the smartest man in this group, holding Detroit in all three of his bets. This morning the Lions' injury report reads like a tax audit. Jared Goff is questionable with a chest injury and Amon-Ra St. Brown with his ribs. The secondary Andy was already patching after Kerby Joseph's knee now has Brian Branch and D.J. Reed questionable with hips. Detroit is still a 2.5-point favourite over New England and Andy is still 82 percent against Darren, so nobody needs a paper bag yet. His 47 percent coin flip with Steve, though, is now two questionable quarterbacks staring at each other. Mahomes is still on the list with an undisclosed problem, and the Chiefs line at Atlanta has slid again, to 3. My read is the market still doesn't trust him. I'd take Goff's chest over whatever Kansas City isn't telling us.

Rob, meanwhile, has managed something special: both of his teams have kicker trouble. Baltimore has signed journeyman Riley Patterson, its third kicker, and Andy Reid says the struggling Harrison Butker is still his man for Sunday. Darren shares Rob's Ravens misery in two bets, but Darren has an escape hatch.

As for yesterday's called shot: I said nobody reads the Bengals' paperwork. Zac Taylor read it, apologised, and said the failed Ebiketie trade "was on our end." Cincinnati is still 12-1 and favoured by 3.5 over Pittsburgh. I'm still taking Darren. Rob, maybe hold the bet slip with both hands.

Steve went into deadline day holding Kansas City in three bets and came out of it with Josh Downs too. The Chiefs pried the receiver loose from the Colts, and Downs marked his move from 2-7 to 6-2 with a Vince Carter GIF. On the same day, Patrick and Brittany Mahomes announced baby No. 4. However, Mahomes is still questionable with that elbow, Xavier Worthy is questionable with a hamstring, and the line at Atlanta has slipped from Chiefs by 4.5 to 3.5. My read is that the market wants to see the elbow throw before it pays for the new receiver.

That matters most to Rob, whose only live ticket is the Chiefs against Darren's Bengals, still at 43 percent. The wind is blowing Darren's way. Joe Burrow has overtaken Josh Allen as MVP favourite, and Cincinnati's title price has shortened from 14-1 to 12-1 while Kansas City drifted out to 10-1. Yes, the Bengals backed out of an agreed trade for Eagles edge rusher Arnold Ebiketie and got tangled in a comp-pick mix-up, but when your quarterback is the MVP favourite, nobody reads the paperwork. I'm taking Darren. Sorry, Rob.

Andy, about that secondary you patched: Kerby Joseph is now out with a knee. Detroit has still moved from a 1.5-point favourite to 2.5 against New England, so I'm keeping my pick, just holding on tighter. Baltimore traded for a center and got made a bigger favourite against the Chargers, Kyle Hamilton's hip notwithstanding. That's very nice for a team I buried yesterday.

The Ravens have handed the keys to Jacoby Brissett, and Jamison Hensley is openly asking whether Lamar Jackson takes them back at all this season. Lamar is on injured reserve with his thumb, Baltimore is 4-5, and the market has pushed the Ravens out from 125-1 to 150-1. Rob and Darren each hold Baltimore against both Andy and Steve, so four of this pool's six bets now ride on a backup and a prayer. Rob sits at 17 percent against Andy and 13 against Steve, and Darren has exactly the same numbers. I think those figures are still being polite. A 4-5 team without Lamar, now missing Jaylinn Hawkins and Nate Wiggins from the secondary, isn't going farther than anybody.

Yesterday I called Rob's portfolio a waiting room. Today the doctor came out and told him to take a seat. His one lifeline is Kansas City against Darren, and that has slipped to 43 percent with Mahomes day-to-day on his throwing elbow. Darren is at least hedged: he loses the Ravens bets alongside Rob, but he has Joe Burrow, and Rob doesn't.

Andy, meanwhile, went shopping. The Lions sent a draft pick to the Jets for safety Andre Cisco to patch their battered secondary, and Andy versus Steve has ticked to 46-54. I took Andy's side yesterday. One point isn't vindication, but I'll be insufferable about it anyway.

Patrick Mahomes is on the injury report this morning, questionable with an elbow problem. The Chiefs still won on Sunday because Kenneth Walker III came up huge after Mahomes got hurt. Steve's whole method is doing nothing, and now he has to do nothing while nervous. He's at 87 percent against Rob and against Darren, but only 55 against Andy. The market barely blinked, easing Kansas City from 9.5-1 to 10-1. I think it's being generous. Harrison Butker leads the league with seven missed field goals, and Andy Reid won't say whether he keeps his job. A team with a questionable quarterback and a kicker on trial looks to me like a 10-1 team on Walker's back and nothing else.

Rob also holds Kansas City against Darren, so both of his quarterbacks are now on an injury list. That isn't a portfolio. It's a waiting room.

Andy's Lions ground out a 19-9 win over Miami, and Jake Bates kicked four field goals, which Steve should frame and hang over Butker's locker. The defence is falling apart, though. Jack Campbell is on injured reserve, and Kerby Joseph, D.J. Reed and DJ Wonnum are all out. Andy versus Steve at 45-55 is the bet to watch, and I'd take Andy's side of it today.

As for my called shot: I told Darren to hold his lead loosely. Joe Burrow then won his fourth straight, Cincinnati shortened to 12-1, and Darren now leads Rob 56-44. Pittsburgh is next. Consider my advice withdrawn.

Lamar Jackson went on injured reserve this morning with his thumb. In the same breath, he told his Ravens teammates he plans to come back later this season. Rob and Darren will read that as a lifeline. I read it as a man promising to move back into a house that is still on fire. Baltimore hasn't reached 14 points in four straight games and sits at 150-1, and the one player who might fix that is now officially parked. Rob is at 19 percent against Andy and 14 against Steve, and Darren is at 14 against Steve. Those numbers belong on a drip, not in a trophy case. The dead cat has announced a comeback tour.

Darren has a second front to worry about. Kyle Dugger was ruled out for Cincinnati today, and the line at Atlanta has shrunk from 4.5 points to 3 since it opened. Yet the Bengals' title odds have shortened to 14-1, so the market either can't make up its mind or is hedging. My read is that Madrid glamour doesn't cover for a thin secondary. Ja'Marr Chase walking into Jessie Bates's building makes for a lovely storyline and a nervy afternoon. Darren leads Rob 54 to 46 in that bet, and I'd hold the lead loosely.

Meanwhile Steve is at 86 percent against both Rob and Darren. His Chiefs are 9.5-point favourites over the Jets, and he has once again done nothing at all. It keeps working, and I hate that it keeps working.

Baltimore's answer to losing both its quarterbacks is Jacoby Brissett, bought for a 2027 fourth-round pick and a 2028 seventh, with a fifth coming back. The Ravens' own coverage is selling him as "hope but realistic expectations," which is what you say once the soufflé has already collapsed. They have scored fewer than 14 points in four straight games, Derrick Henry isn't going anywhere, and the bookmakers have pushed them out again, to 150-1. Donte Whitner calls firing John Harbaugh a "catastrophic mistake." I'd say the whole season is one. Rob has slipped again against Andy, from 20 percent to 19. The dead-cat bounce I called is now just a dead cat.

Andy should check his own sick bay before he gloats. Jack Campbell, doubtful yesterday, has now been ruled out, along with Kerby Joseph, D.J. Reed, DJ Wonnum and centre Cade Mays. Amon-Ra St. Brown is questionable with sore ribs. That's half a defence on the trip to Miami, and Detroit has drifted to 19-1. He's still at 81 percent, so expect him to be insufferable either way.

The only people having fun are in Madrid, where the Bengals reportedly drew their biggest practice crowd ever and Joe Burrow went looking at art. Cincinnati has shortened to 14-1. Steve's Chiefs have eased to 10-1 and will face the Jets without Mansoor Delane and Peter Woods. Darren leads Rob 54 to 46 in that bet, and my hunch is that Burrow's European tour widens the gap. Steve sits at 86 percent and still does nothing, which at this point is clearly his strategy.

Thursday night in Baltimore went about as badly as it could for Rob and Darren. In the rain, Jacksonville beat the Ravens 33-10 and never trailed. With their top two quarterbacks injured, Baltimore spent a good part of the night snapping the ball straight to Derrick Henry. Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley are both on injured reserve now, and the team is 4-5. Henry passed LaDainian Tomlinson for seventh on the all-time rushing list, which makes him the only Raven having a good week. The team says the slump can't be pinned on losing Jackson. That's meant to sound brave, but I think it's the worst news of the lot, because it means they think they're this bad anyway. The bookmakers have pushed Baltimore out to 125-1.

Yesterday I called Rob and Darren's small rise against Andy a dead-cat bounce, and it has already dropped back from 23 percent to 20. Both men are at 14 percent against Steve. Steve is now at 86 and is doing nothing at all to earn it.

Andy shouldn't get smug. Kerby Joseph is out, Jack Campbell is doubtful with his neck, and the Miami line slipped from seven points to six and a half on Friday. My guess is the market has noticed Detroit's thinning defence. Darren still leads Rob 54 to 46 in the Bengals-Chiefs bet, so my called shot is holding. Rob, your Chiefs are the only lifeline you have left. I'd start being nice to them.

The Baltimore Ravens were down to their third-string quarterback, so they've gone shopping. Sources say they're finalising a trade with Arizona for Jacoby Brissett. Tyler Huntley has gone from doubtful to out, which means rookie Joe Fagnano starts tonight against Jacksonville, and his career begins with two games in five days. The bookmakers responded by pushing Baltimore's title odds from 40-1 to 100-1. Rob and Darren have edged up from 20 to 23 percent against Andy, which I'd call a dead-cat bounce. Brissett is a sensible veteran, but I don't think a sensible veteran saves a 4-4 team. Even the friendly coverage says it "remains to be seen." Rob holds Baltimore against two friends, and I'd bet he spent breakfast refreshing Arizona's transactions page.

Andy's injury list got longer. Amon-Ra St. Brown is questionable with his ribs and Brian Branch with a concussion. The best news of the week is Jack Campbell's statement that he has full movement in his lower body, and that matters more than any bet. Against the two Ravens holders, Andy is fine. Against Steve he's at 44 percent, and the Lions without their best receiver look a lot more ordinary.

Steve is sitting pretty at 82 against both Baltimore holders. Even so, Travis Kelce and Rashee Rice are both questionable, and Chris Jones has half a sack in seven games. Jones says he isn't worried. Annoyingly, Steve doesn't need to be either. My called shot is holding: Cincinnati's title odds have shortened to 14-1, and Darren is still at 55 percent against Rob's Chiefs. I'm not saying I told you so, Rob. Not yet.

The Ravens opened this week as 4.5-point favourites at home to Jacksonville. They are now ten-point underdogs. That's a 14.5-point swing, and I think it's the quarterback room the market is pricing. Jesse Minter confirmed Tuesday that rookie Joe Fagnano will make his first NFL start Thursday night. Tyler Huntley has slipped from questionable to doubtful with his toe. For good measure, kicker Tyler Loop has gone on injured reserve, so Jake Moody is moving up the depth chart as well. Baltimore is now without its starting quarterback, very likely its backup, and its kicker. Rob and Darren have each slipped to 20 percent against Andy. Steve hasn't moved off 84 against either of them. The flowers to Baltimore are still a good idea, Steve, and Fagnano deserves a fruit basket.

Andy should be careful about gloating. Kerby Joseph is out, Jack Campbell is doubtful with the neck injury, and Jimmy Rolder has gone on IR. The market doesn't care: Detroit moved from 6.5 to 7 points at Miami. Against two Ravens bets, Andy is fine. Against Steve's Chiefs, at 45 percent, a thinning Lions defence is the thing I'd worry about.

My called shot has a wobble. Yesterday I took Darren's Bengals over Rob's Chiefs. Since then, Cincinnati's line at Atlanta has shrunk from 4.5 points to 3, and DJ Turner and Kyle Dugger are both questionable. I'm sticking with it, mostly because I won't give Rob the satisfaction.

The Ravens' title odds didn't drift this time, they collapsed: from +4000 to +10000 in two days. The talk has moved on from Lamar Jackson's thumb to whether he'll ever play for Baltimore again, and one report says it's possible his last snap as a Raven has already happened. Thursday's best hope is Joe Fagnano, who has an ankle injury and, according to Jesse Minter, "a chance" to play. Tyler Huntley is still questionable with his toe. Yesterday I said the numbers flattered Rob and Darren, and overnight the numbers agreed. Rob is down to 22 percent against Andy and 16 against Steve. Darren is at 16 against Steve and 22 against Andy. These aren't bets anymore. They're souvenirs.

Darren gets a special kind of torment. Trey Hendrickson has two sacks in Baltimore, but the three players Cincinnati brought in to replace him have 13.5 between them. Darren holds both teams, so he's watching his Bengals prove the Ravens bought the wrong pass rusher. Cincinnati shortened to +1400 even with Cashius Howell out indefinitely after wrist surgery. Rob's Chiefs against Darren's Bengals sits at 45 percent, and I'd take Darren.

Before Sunday, Kansas City was 80-2 under Mahomes when leading by ten or more in the fourth quarter. Now the Chiefs are +1000 and second in the AFC West. Steve, still sitting at 84 percent against two quarterback-less Ravens bets, should send Baltimore flowers. And the best news of the day: Jack Campbell is still in hospital, but the Lions say early signs are positive.

Yesterday Lamar Jackson was the man Rob and Darren were counting on. This morning he is headed to injured reserve with a thumb injury, and Tyler Huntley, next in line, is questionable with a toe. The Ravens drifted from +3500 to +4000 for the title. Baltimore appears in four of the six bets on this page, all held by Rob or Darren, and they now look like four bets with nobody throwing the ball. Rob sits at 31 percent against Andy and 25 against Steve, and Darren at 25 against Steve. If anything, those numbers flatter them.

Yesterday I took the Broncos, mostly out of spite. Kansas City reached the Denver 4-yard line with 35 seconds left, ran five straight plays without scoring, and Roach sacked Mahomes on fourth-and-goal to seal a 28-24 Denver win. Spite has never felt so much like analysis. The Chiefs drifted to +950, and Steve, who holds them in all three bets, is now leaning on Baltimore's quarterback room more than on Mahomes. Meanwhile Joe Burrow threw five touchdown passes, then ran one in himself in overtime to beat Tennessee 43-36, and Cincinnati shortened to +1500. That makes Rob, holding Kansas City against Darren's Bengals at 46 percent, the only man on this page to lose twice in one afternoon.

I also called Andy quietly doomed yesterday. He is now 69 percent against Darren, so that call blew up. The sour note is Jack Campbell, carted off on a backboard and now doubtful with a neck injury. Here's hoping he's fine. Detroit shortened anyway.

Yesterday L'Jarius Sneed and Mansoor Delane were merely questionable, and I was hoping Bo Nix might rescue my low opinion of Kansas City. This morning Sneed is on injured reserve and Delane is out, so the Chiefs go to Denver two cornerbacks short and still giving 1.5 points. I think that number is asleep, and I'm taking the Broncos, partly on analysis and mostly out of spite. Steve holds Kansas City in all three bets and sits at 64 or 65 percent in each. Those are the fattest prices on this page and, to my eye, the softest.

The quiet profiteer is Darren, who has Baltimore against Steve and Cincinnati against Rob, so two of Darren's three bets improve as the Chiefs' secondary shrinks. Tee Higgins is having one of the best seasons of his career, and the Bengals have gone from 6.5-point to 12.5-point favourites against Tennessee. Rob holds Kansas City against Darren and Baltimore against Steve, and so gets to mourn and celebrate the same injury report.

Nobody should get giddy about the Ravens, though. They went from +3 to +3.5 at Buffalo today, the same day T.J. Tampa landed on the list as questionable. My read is that the two are connected, and I'm still calling that Baltimore loss. Andy is the underdog in all three bets and quietly doomed, yet Detroit has shortened to +2100 for the title. I can only assume the market has seen the uniforms.

Lamar Jackson will play in Buffalo on Sunday and calls the pain in his left ankle "bearable," a word I associate with airline food rather than a franchise quarterback. It is still the best news Rob and Darren have had all week, since each holds the Ravens against both Andy and Steve. Now the catch: guard Olaivavega Ioane has gone from questionable to out with his MCL, and safety Jaylinn Hawkins is out too. Yesterday I said Jackson may get a thinner line. Strike "may." A sore quarterback, a patched line and a depleted secondary against Josh Allen still looks to me like the Baltimore loss I called. The Ravens have been getting 3 points since Wednesday, and my read is that the market isn't swooning over one adjective.

The softest number on this page got a little firmer, and I don't enjoy typing that. Rashee Rice is expected back from his hamstring for Denver, which helps Steve in all three of his bets. L'Jarius Sneed and Mansoor Delane are both questionable, so Bo Nix may yet rescue my opinion. Rob holds Kansas City against Darren and bets against it with Baltimore, making him the only man here who can't decide how to feel about Rice.

Andy, meanwhile, has lost Kerby Joseph for the Vikings game and Isiah Pacheco to injured reserve, with Roger McCreary questionable. Detroit has shrunk from 4.5-point favourite to 3 against the league's only unbeaten team. At least the Rivalries uniform is reporting no limitations.

Travis Kelce has an ankle, Rashee Rice has a hamstring, and both are questionable for Sunday's first-place game in Denver, where Patrick Mahomes is still grinding through his own injury comeback. Tackle Jaylon Moore is questionable as well, with a concussion. Steve has Kansas City in all three of his bets and sits at 64 or 65 percent in each, which I think is the softest number on this page. The market disagrees: the Chiefs opened as 1.5-point underdogs and are now 1.5-point favourites. Dave Toub, meanwhile, declared emphatically that Harrison Butker is still the kicker. Nothing says job security like a coordinator having to say so with Justin Tucker on the practice squad.

Yesterday I called a Buffalo shootout that Baltimore loses, and the Ravens keep helping. Cornerback T.J. Tampa went on injured reserve today and guard Olaivavega Ioane is questionable with an MCL problem, so Josh Allen gets a thinner secondary and Lamar Jackson, himself still listed as questionable, may get a thinner line. Rob holds both the Ravens and the Chiefs, which gives him the two longest injury lists I have and very little to enjoy over coffee.

The line that lurched is Darren's. Cincinnati opened at 6.5 over Tennessee and moved to 12.5 today, even with receiver Andrei Iosivas going on injured reserve. That Bengals bet against Rob is only 43 percent, and I'd buy it. Andy is the quiet disaster: underdog in all three bets, hosting the league's only unbeaten team, and debuting a Rivalries uniform. He will lose well dressed.

Lamar Jackson was a full participant in Wednesday's practice, and Rob and Darren breathed out across four separate bets. They shouldn't get comfortable. This morning Kyle Hamilton and Roquan Smith joined the questionable list with knee problems, and running back Adam Randall went on injured reserve. That is the defense Solak filed under "struggling," and it may now be without the two players I would least like to lose. A healthy Lamar is lovely. A healthy Lamar trading touchdowns in Buffalo behind a patched line, with half a defense, is not a plan. I think it's a shootout Baltimore loses.

Andy shouldn't look smug either. Jahmyr Gibbs spent the week talking about fully taking over the Lions' backfield, and he is now questionable with a shoulder. Amon-Ra St. Brown has an ankle, and Kerby Joseph is out. The Minnesota line has slid from 4.5 to 3. My read is that's the injury report talking, although the title price somehow shortened anyway. Andy versus Darren sits at 48 to 52, two limping teams in a coin flip.

Steve keeps collecting bad news and remains the favourite regardless. Defensive tackle Omarr Norman-Lott is out with an ACL injury, L'Jarius Sneed is questionable, and the title odds have drifted from +850 to +900. Kansas City's response was to put Justin Tucker on the practice squad. Darren, meanwhile, has Ja'Marr Chase questionable with an ankle, and Rob will be checking on that ankle more often than Darren will.

The Ravens have lost the man who was supposed to stand in front of Lamar Jackson's ankle. Rookie guard Olaivavega Ioane sprained his MCL in Sunday's loss to the Bengals and is now listed doubtful. Broderick Washington Jr. and Jaylinn Hawkins have joined Lamar on the questionable list. Rob and Darren hold Baltimore in four bets between them, and they would like a word with whoever is writing "complicated injury history" features this week. Oddly, the Buffalo line came in from +3.5 to +3 today, the same day Ioane was listed. My read is that the market is betting on Lamar playing and doesn't much care who blocks for him. I do. Yesterday I said the first half was never the problem. Solak now files the Ravens' defense under "struggling," and I am claiming that one.

Darren had the rare pleasure of winning and losing the same game on Sunday, because his Bengals beat his own Ravens. The bill came Tuesday: tight end Erick All Jr. went on injured reserve with what is believed to be a torn ACL. The market shrugged and made Cincinnati a ten-point favourite over Tennessee. Rob, 57% in that bet with the Chiefs, is not sending flowers.

Steve's Chiefs have Rashee Rice questionable with a hamstring and Jaylon Moore with a concussion, and Solak is floating a receiver trade. Somehow they have gone from underdogs to 1.5-point favourites in Denver. Steve is still favourite against all three of his friends, and I am still not convinced.

Lamar Jackson might be back. Ravens coach Jesse Minter said Monday he is optimistic his quarterback can play the Bills on Sunday, and the ankle has gone from out to questionable. Rob and Darren, who hold the Ravens against both Andy and Steve, can breathe again. Not too deeply, though. The bookmakers heard the same news and still pushed Baltimore out to +1300. The Ravens have outscored teams by 65 points in first halves and been outscored by 70 after the break, which makes them the best first-half team in the league and the worst second-half one. My view is that Lamar fixes the first half, and the first half was never the problem.

Kansas City's hangover got worse. Nate Taylor says the Chiefs struggled in all three phases in Seattle, Stephen A. Smith is stunned by the offense, and their title odds slid again to +900. Yesterday I told Steve to enjoy being 64% favourite while it lasts. It has lasted another day, and I am starting to look silly. He is still close to two-to-one against all three of his friends. Darren, meanwhile, watched his Bengals shorten to +1600 even with Kyle Dugger ruled out, and is now the only one whose teams both moved the right way.

Andy should enjoy yesterday's luck while he can. Amon-Ra St. Brown is questionable with an ankle, and in my opinion a Lions offense without him is Jared Goff and a prayer. Solak is talking up Goff as an MVP candidate. Andy will need him to be one.

Ja'Marr Chase lost his temper at halftime, and Rob lost a lot more. Chase unloaded on his Bengals teammates at the break, Cincinnati came back to beat Baltimore, and the Ravens' own beat reporter is calling it a blowout. Yesterday this column said Darren would have something to cheer about whoever won. He did. The market likes his Bengals too, with their title odds in from +2100 to +1700. Rob's Ravens drifted to +1200, and Lamar Jackson is still listed out with that ankle. Rob also holds Kansas City against Darren, which brings us to the bad news.

Steve's Chiefs are no longer perfect. Seattle beat them 20-3 on Sunday night. Jaxon Smith-Njigba had 150 yards, and Kenneth Walker III had his worst game of the season. Then the Seahawks finished the job by trolling Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce online. Rashee Rice is out with a hamstring, and Kansas City has drifted to +850. Yesterday I called them a team with standards. Three points is not a standard. Steve should enjoy being 64% favourite while it lasts.

Andy is the quiet winner. Dan Campbell's fourth-down gamble failed, and the Lions still beat Green Bay 20-17 with a field goal on the last play, helped by a few flags that went their way. Detroit is in to +2100, and Andy's chances against Steve have climbed from 28% to 35%. Was it lucky? Absolutely. Luck still counts.

Rob, the praying didn't work. The Ravens have ruled Lamar Jackson out against Cincinnati with that high ankle sprain, and Tyler "Snoop" Huntley gets the start. The bookmakers seem to have smelled it early. Baltimore opened as a 3.5-point favourite, was a 1.5-point underdog until Saturday, and is now getting three points at home. My read is that the market knew before the Ravens said so. Rob holds Baltimore against Andy and Steve, and so does Darren. But Darren also holds Cincinnati against Rob, so whoever wins today, Darren has something to cheer about. Smug, Darren. Very smug.

Steve's Chiefs had a locker-room moment of their own. Sources say Andy Reid and Patrick Mahomes threw tackle Josh Simmons out of a team meeting, and Simmons later apologised. To me that looks like a team with standards, not a team in crisis. The market seems to agree: Kansas City's title odds have shortened to +750 this week, even though running back Brashard Smith has gone on injured reserve and L'Jarius Sneed is questionable. Nobody seems to care, least of all Steve, who stays insufferable.

Andy has to face Josh Jacobs, who makes his season debut for Green Bay against the Lions. Even so, Detroit moved out to 3.5-point favourites this morning. The Lions are wearing all black today, which suits a man who's 28% against Steve.

Yesterday this column announced that the bookmakers had quietly decided Lamar Jackson would play. Then Lamar spoke, and they changed their minds. He says it's a high ankle sprain and he's unsure whether he'll face Cincinnati on Sunday after missing the past two games. The best he would offer was "heading in the right direction." Baltimore has gone from 1.5-point favourites to 1.5-point underdogs at home. My read is that the line moved because of what he said. He's still listed as questionable, and the Ravens have also ruled out safety Jaylinn Hawkins and linebacker Tavius Robinson. Rob holds Baltimore against both Andy and Steve, so he can stop hoping and go back to praying.

Andy had a lousy Friday too. Lions safety Brian Branch is out with an Achilles injury, and centre Cade Mays has gone on injured reserve. Sam LaPorta also complained in public about his contract, then softened his tone while Dan Campbell played it down. Andy's only comfort is that Green Bay will be without linebacker Zaire Franklin. A man who's 28% against Steve takes whatever he can get.

Steve isn't untouched either. Rashee Rice is out with a hamstring, and tackle Jaylon Moore is out with a concussion, a week after Josh Simmons went on injured reserve. Kansas City are now 3-point underdogs in Seattle. Still, I would rather have Kenneth Walker III running behind a patched-up line than have Rob's quarterback's ankle. Steve is still sitting prettiest, and the rest of you are hoping for bad news to come his way.

The bookmakers have changed their minds about Lamar Jackson's ankle. After the limp knocked Baltimore from 3.5-point favourites to 1.5-point underdogs, the line has swung back, and the Ravens are 1.5-point favourites over Cincinnati again. Jackson is still officially questionable, so the market hasn't been told anything we haven't. My read is that it has quietly decided he plays. Marlon Humphrey is already defending him, complaining about "slander" against his quarterback. The catch is that centre Cam Jurgens is questionable with a concussion, so even a healthy Lamar might be taking snaps from a stranger. Trey Hendrickson, finally looking healthier, insists his first game against his old team is "not about me." It is entirely about him. Rob has gone from praying to merely hoping. Darren owns a piece of both teams, so he can watch Sunday with no feelings at all.

Steve's Chiefs have put left tackle Josh Simmons on injured reserve, which should hurt. But Kenneth Walker III is on a historic pace and goes back to Seattle to face the team that let him go, and Kansas City's title price has shortened to +750. I'd rather be Steve than anyone else in this pool, and it isn't close.

Andy's Lions are now three-point favourites over Green Bay, up from 1.5, and they're wearing all black. That may be the right outfit for a man with a 28% chance against Steve.

Lamar Jackson is back at practice, then walked into the building limping on his left ankle, and Baltimore still won't say whether he plays the Bengals on Sunday. This column had him out yesterday. The injury list now calls him questionable, and cornerback T.J. Tampa has gone to injured reserve. The bookmakers haven't waited for an answer. The Ravens opened as 3.5-point home favourites and are now 1.5-point underdogs, and my read is that the limp did that. Rob holds Baltimore against Andy and against Steve, and a Bengals win also helps Darren against Rob's Chiefs. Nobody in this pool needs Lamar's ankle more than Rob. Darren holds the Ravens twice and the Bengals once, so he wins something whatever happens Sunday. That isn't strategy. Darren just bought one of everything.

Andy's morning is confusing. One report says safety Brian Branch is coming back for the Packers game, while the injury list has him out with an Achilles. I'd trust the list. Tight end Sam LaPorta says the Lions are "not showing the love" and that he'd be fine playing elsewhere in 2027. Andy has a 28% chance against Steve, so he knows how LaPorta feels.

Steve has Travis Kelce, Rashee Rice and L'Jarius Sneed all questionable, and the Chiefs have drifted from 2.5 to 3-point underdogs in Seattle. Xavier Worthy keeps growing into a bigger role, though, and I think an unbeaten team with a spare receiver is still the best seat in the house. Steve is sitting pretty. Rob is praying.

Lamar Jackson is now listed as out with his ankle, even though the Ravens' own reporting still calls him day-to-day. He has company. Center Cam Jurgens is out with a concussion, guard Andrew Vorhees and tight end Matt Hibner are out, and Rashod Bateman is questionable. That's the quarterback, the man who snaps him the ball and a chunk of the line, all in the trainer's room. ESPN picked this week to publish a piece on why Baltimore is the league's worst team at blowing double-digit leads, under the headline "It's Groundhog Day." The bookmakers eased the Ravens out from +950 to +1000. Rob and Darren each hold Baltimore twice. In my view, a Ravens team without Lamar has finally run out of ways to build a lead worth blowing.

Steve, meanwhile, owns the only unbeaten team in this pool. The Chiefs are 5-0, just as this column insisted they would stay, and their title price shortened again to +750. Rashee Rice and tackle Josh Simmons are out, and Steve won't lose a minute's sleep over either. Rob's best asset this morning is his Chiefs bet against Darren, which makes him the one man here quietly hoping Steve keeps winning.

Darren, I said the market was moving his chair closer to the door. It's now in the hallway: the Bengals drifted to +2100 and lost tight end Tanner Hudson to injured reserve. Andy's Lions got slightly shorter odds without doing anything, which is basically Andy's whole strategy.

Nothing juicy broke overnight. The new items are ESPN counting down to a Super Bowl four months away, a list of great rookie Super Bowl performances, and a guide to what every team is wearing this week. The injury report that ruined Friday for Rob and Darren hasn't changed since. So the morning's prize goes to Darren. A day after ESPN called his Bengals "overperforming," it has published a piece on how they can improve after their bye. They're overperforming and they still have homework. Their title odds have drifted from +1700 to +1900 over the past three weeks, which looks to me like the market quietly moving his chair closer to the door.

Andy gets a rare quiet morning, mostly because his Lions aren't playing. He's below a third in all three of his bets. The best thing that can happen to Andy today is nothing, and he's getting it.

The waiting ends this afternoon. Tyler Huntley takes the Ravens to Cleveland to face Todd Monken. Yesterday I backed Monken, and I'm not taking it back. Then it's Mahomes against Herbert with Rashee Rice out. I still say the Chiefs win, and Steve keeps smiling. Rob has the strangest Sunday of the four. He holds Baltimore against Andy and Steve and Kansas City against Darren, so my predicted afternoon has him cheering and wincing at the same time. Darren needs Huntley too, which is a sentence nobody wants to read about their own money.

Lamar Jackson is officially out. The ankle that was "questionable" in yesterday's column has ruled him out for a second straight week, so Tyler Huntley starts in Cleveland. Waiting on the other sideline is Todd Monken, the Ravens' own former offensive coordinator, who the Ravens believe wants "to kick our tail." Cam Jurgens has gone from questionable to out with his concussion, and Broderick Washington Jr. and Matt Hibner are out too. The line that opened at 6.5 is now 3. Yesterday I said I was with the market. The market kept walking, and I'm still with it. Kyle Hamilton says everybody has "the utmost confidence" in Huntley, which is the kind of thing teammates say. Rob and Darren have four bets on a backup quarterback facing a coach who knows the playbook. My hunch: Monken has been waiting for this one.

Steve, don't get smug. Rashee Rice is now officially out against the Chargers, tackle Josh Simmons is out with a back injury and L'Jarius Sneed is questionable. Still, Kansas City is a 7.5-point favourite against a team that hasn't won a game, and I think the Chiefs stay unbeaten. Steve holds them against all three of his friends, so he's the one sitting pretty.

Andy, your Lions are on a bye and still put three players on injured reserve: Ben Bartch, Devin White and Tom Kennedy. That's quite something for a week off. Darren, ESPN says your Bengals are "overperforming." I know you'll read that as a compliment. Rob is 62% on that bet and won't.

Remember yesterday, when this column told Rob and Darren they could stop refreshing the injury report? Keep refreshing. Lamar Jackson went on the list Thursday as questionable with that ankle, and the Ravens now head to Cleveland "likely with Huntley at QB." The Baltimore line opened at 6.5, sat at 5.5 and has now slid to 3.5. My read is that the market got the news and stopped believing, and this time I'm with the market. Ja'Kobi Lane, cheerfully back at practice in the last column, is now on injured reserve with a wrist. Cam Jurgens is questionable with a concussion, Zay Flowers with a toe and Rashod Bateman with a shoulder. That isn't an injury report, it's a roll call. Rob and Darren have four bets riding on this team. I'd lock the medicine cabinet.

Steve, the 8.5 is gone, as predicted. Kansas City is now 7.5 against the winless Chargers, a day after Rashee Rice was listed questionable with that hamstring. I think the two are connected, and the Chiefs are still a full-touchdown favourite. They're the last unbeaten team in the AFC, and with Baltimore limping, I think Steve's two coin flips against Rob and Darren are tipping his way, pass rush or no pass rush.

Andy's Lions stay unbeaten for another week by not playing, and someone has ranked the NFC North the best division in football. Andy, stick that on the fridge. It's the best news you'll get all month.

Lamar Jackson has a realistic chance to play Sunday in Cleveland, a league source told ESPN, even though he didn't practise Wednesday. Trey Hendrickson and Cam Jurgens were back at practice as well. The Baltimore line sat at 4.5 until Wednesday and is now back to 5.5. Yesterday this column guessed the market didn't trust Jackson's ankle. My read is that it has started trusting it again, and the timing fits. Rob and Darren hold the Ravens in four bets between them, so they can stop refreshing the injury report every ten minutes. I want to see Jackson actually take a snap before anyone gets cocky. Still, a 4-1 team getting its quarterback back is a team I'd rather hold than bet against.

Steve, enjoy that 8.5-point line while it lasts. The Chiefs haven't recorded a sack since Week 1, and coming into this week they ranked 27th in pass rush win rate. The club says it still has faith in the pass rush, which is what clubs always say. Rashee Rice is also questionable with a bad hamstring. To me, a 4-0 team with no pass rush looks like it's living on borrowed time, and I think Rob and Darren's 52% against Steve is on the low side.

Andy's Lions are on their bye, so for the first time all season they're guaranteed not to lose. They found "some much-needed momentum" in Arizona, apparently. Andy, rest up and enjoy it.

Somebody out there really likes the Kansas City Chiefs. Their line against the Chargers opened at 2.5 points and now sits at 8.5. That six-point lurch is the loudest noise on this page this week. Yesterday this column found a "crack" in Steve's empire because Kansas City's title price drifted from +900 to +950. The point spread has since moved six points the other way. Steve holds the Chiefs in three bets and has done nothing all season but sit there, so he has earned a smug cup of coffee. I still think Rob and Darren's 52% against him is fair value, but I would say it more quietly today.

First, a correction. Lamar Jackson, Cam Jurgens, Andrew Vorhees and Trey Hendrickson are listed as questionable, not out as this column claimed. That's better news for Rob and Darren. The line in Cleveland has still slid from 6.5 points to 4.5. My guess is that the market doesn't trust Jackson's ankle, though nobody has said so.

Darren's Bengals have lost tight end Tanner Hudson for the season. He tore a pectoral in Sunday's win over the Dolphins, and Swayze Bozeman has gone on injured reserve. Cincinnati's title price has drifted out to +1900. Darren holds the Bengals only against Rob, and Rob's Chiefs are 4-0 against a 3-2 team that keeps losing players. Darren, frame the Baltimore tickets. Andy, there's nothing new to report, which is the best news you've had all week.

The Kansas City Chiefs are 4-0, and the bookmakers are still edging away from them. Their title price drifted from +900 to +950 overnight, and Tyquan Thornton went on injured reserve. Yesterday this column said Steve couldn't keep winning by doing nothing forever. The first crack has come from the betting market rather than the field, but a crack is a crack. Steve holds Kansas City in three bets, and the people setting the prices have just gone a little cooler on all of them. Baltimore, meanwhile, shortened to +800 with its backup quarterback. My hunch is that Rob and Darren's 52% against Steve is now the cheapest ticket on this page.

That said, the Ravens' injury report is starting to look like a hospital bill. Lamar Jackson, Cam Jurgens, Andrew Vorhees and Trey Hendrickson are all listed out, and Ja'Kobi Lane is on injured reserve. Four tickets are riding on Tyler Huntley and whoever is still standing. The market doesn't seem bothered. I'm a little bothered.

Andy's Lions just lost Tom Kennedy for the season. Ben Bartch and Rock Ya-Sin are out and Devin White is doubtful, so 28% and 31% look generous, whatever the shorter title odds say. Samaje Perine gave Darren's Bengals a jolt, but Colbie Young and Kyle Dugger are both out. Rob holds both Baltimore and Kansas City, which makes him the nearest thing this group has to a hedge fund. Smug, but correct.

Yesterday this column looked at Snoop Huntley carrying four Ravens tickets into Atlanta and said Steve's side of the coin was the one to take. Huntley then went 11-for-11 for 80 yards on the last two drives, forced overtime and scored the winner himself on a one-yard run, 30-23. Lamar is still out, Cam Jurgens is still concussed, and the Ravens are 4-1 anyway. Rob and Darren each still sit at 52% against Steve, which feels stingy for men whose backup quarterback won't throw an incompletion. Steve, meanwhile, keeps winning by doing nothing at all. That can't last forever, and I suspect he knows it.

This column was also wrong about Detroit. It said 5.5 points was too many, and the Lions won 45-21, with Jahmyr Gibbs passing Barry Sanders for the most touchdowns before age 25. Dan Campbell admitted he felt the season teetering, so give him credit for finding the edge and stepping back. Andy's reward is 28% against Darren and 31% against Steve. The hobby has become a slightly better-funded hobby.

Darren's Bengals beat Miami 31-24 behind four Burrow touchdowns, and even the Bengals say they weren't happy with how they played. Rob is up to 72% against Andy and is still the man to beat. If Huntley keeps this up, Rob's two Ravens tickets go from his worry to his best asset.

Nothing blew up overnight, so this morning's lead is paperwork. League sources say the Ravens insisted Cam Jurgens pass a physical in Philadelphia before they would finalise the trade for him. Very thorough. He is now out with a concussion, Lamar is still out, and Zay Flowers is still questionable, so Baltimore's medical due diligence is the one part of the operation nobody can fault. Tonight Snoop Huntley carries four tickets into Atlanta for Rob and Darren. Rob at least has Kansas City as a lifeboat. Darren's lifeboat is the Bengals, and Ja'Marr Chase is still listed with a concussion.

Andy also has news about a centre, which is as close as he gets to good news these days. Cade Mays has gone on injured reserve with a wrist, a detail this column missed yesterday while counting the holes in Detroit's secondary. The bright spot is Drew Petzing, whose time in Arizona might help against the Cardinals. My hunch is that inside knowledge is worth about a field goal, so yesterday's call that 5.5 points is too many still stands. Andy is at roughly 30% in all three of his bets, which is less a position than a hobby.

Steve has had no new names on the Kansas City injury list for three days running. He is 4-0 and a coin flip against both Ravens holders, and on a day when Huntley is the quarterback I'd take his side of that coin. Rob is sitting at 70% against Andy and 64% against Darren, and he's the man to beat. The only thing that worries me on his behalf is that he's holding two Ravens tickets.

Lamar Jackson is out. The Ravens have ruled him out of Sunday night in Atlanta, so Snoop Huntley starts against a Falcons team that is reportedly feeling confident with Michael Penix Jr. at quarterback. Jesse Minter says he expects Huntley to play well, which is what anyone would say about the backup on Saturday. It gets worse. Cam Jurgens is out with a concussion, Trey Hendrickson has gone from questionable to out with his finger, Ja'Kobi Lane is on injured reserve and Zay Flowers is questionable with a foot. Yesterday this column trusted the gloomy Sunday price over the cheerful February one, and that call looks healthier than Baltimore's roster. Oddly, the line has come in from +3.5 to +3. My guess is the market had already assumed Lamar wouldn't play. Rob and Darren hold four Baltimore tickets between them. I would not want any of them this weekend.

Andy's candle has been snuffed out. Brian Branch is out with an Achilles, and Rock Ya-Sin and Ben Bartch are out too. That leaves a Lions secondary I wouldn't trust against a stiff breeze. Detroit is still giving 5.5 at Arizona, and I think that's too many.

Darren is now on the third chapter of his tragedy. Kyle Dugger is out and Bryan Cook is questionable, so the Bengals are short at safety on top of everything else. Steve, meanwhile, has no new names on Kansas City's injury list for a second day running. He is 4-0 and doing absolutely nothing, which is the most annoying thing a man can do in a pool.

The Ravens opened this week as 4.5-point favourites in Atlanta. They are now 3-point underdogs. That is a seven-and-a-half-point swing, and it lands on a team with Lamar Jackson questionable with his ankle and Marlon Humphrey questionable with a calf. Trey Hendrickson and John Simpson are questionable too, and tight end Durham Smythe has gone to injured reserve with an Achilles. Oddly, the title market has nudged Baltimore in to +850. So the bookies believe in the Ravens for February but not for Sunday night. I'm with the Sunday version. Rob and Darren each hold Baltimore in two bets, and both should be watching Michael Penix Jr. and Bijan Robinson through their fingers.

Darren has it worst, because his other team is Cincinnati. Dexter Lawrence II and B.J. Hill are now questionable on the defensive line, on top of the receiver mess we covered yesterday. Two horses, both limping, and Darren is holding the reins of each.

Andy is having the quietest good week in the pool. The Lions have come back in from +2800 to +2600, and the line at Arizona has firmed from 4.5 to 5.5. Cade Mays is listed on injured reserve, so nobody should start engraving anything. Still, yesterday's flicker of hope has become a modest candle, which by Andy's standards is a bonfire. And Steve? Nothing to report again. The Chiefs are 4-0 with no new names on the injury list, and his feet are still up. Someone should check he's still breathing.

The Ravens answered Lamar's wobbly ankle by trading for two-time Pro Bowl center Cam Jurgens from the Eagles, and Jason Kelce says he's excited to see him back at center. Lovely. The snag is that Jurgens is on Baltimore's injury list, questionable with a concussion. So Rob and Darren's big reinforcement arrives in the same condition as the rest of that building. Zay Flowers, Rashod Bateman and Kyle Hamilton have joined the questionable pile too. I like the trade for January. I don't trust it for Sunday night against Bijan Robinson.

Darren, about that line yesterday's column told you to savour. Ja'Marr Chase is questionable with a concussion, Tee Higgins is questionable with a groin injury, and Cincinnati has slipped from 7-point favourites at Miami back to 6.5. My read is that's the receivers showing up in the price. The Bengals have also drifted out to +1900 for the title. Rob's Chiefs bet against those Bengals was the healthiest thing he owned yesterday. Today it's healthier still.

Andy gets a flicker of hope: the Lions have opened the practice window for Brian Branch and Cade Mays, though Branch is still listed out. Then Sam LaPorta announced that his extension talks are at a "stalemate," and the title market pushed Detroit out to +2800. Andy sits under 30% in all three of his bets. Meanwhile Steve's Chiefs are 4-0 and shortening to +900, and their only new injury worry is a questionable tackle. Steve hasn't had to do anything all week, and it's going perfectly.

Lamar Jackson has a sprained ankle, and sources told NFL Network he has only an outside chance of playing Sunday against the Falcons. Yesterday nobody could say whether he'd play. Now somebody has, and it's not what Rob and Darren wanted to hear. The Ravens opened as 4.5-point favourites in Atlanta and are now 3.5-point underdogs, and my read is that this is the Lamar news showing up in the line. On top of that, Durham Smythe is out with an Achilles, and Trey Hendrickson and Chris Moore are both questionable. The title market moved the Ravens from +900 to +850 since Sunday. I wouldn't treat that as a vote of confidence until it survives this week.

Steve is the winner here without lifting a finger. Steve has the 4-0 Chiefs against the Ravens in two bets, and the other team just lost its quarterback to an ankle. Andy also holds two bets against Baltimore. That 30% against Darren now looks less like charity and more like a lottery ticket that's started to tingle. Yesterday this column told Rob to pick a lane. Fate has picked it for him, and his Chiefs bet against Darren is now the healthiest thing he owns.

Darren is quietly doomed. Darren holds the Ravens in two bets and the Bengals against Rob, and Stephen A. is asking out loud why Zac Taylor isn't under more scrutiny. Cincinnati has gone from 5.5-point to 7-point favourites at Miami. That's the only line on this page moving Darren's way, so savour it, Darren. And keep the Falcons tape handy, though it may now be a horror film.

Tyreek Hill is a free agent. His agent, Drew Rosenhaus, says Hill could sign somewhere "over the next few days," and the Chiefs are believed to be interested. Kansas City has been following his rehab since before Tyquan Thornton dislocated his ankle, which now means 12 to 16 weeks out, and before Rashee Rice went questionable with a hamstring. Nothing is signed yet. The bookies have still nudged the Chiefs from +950 to +900, and my hunch is that a 4-0 team adding a familiar speed merchant is the scariest thing on this page. Steve holds Kansas City in three bets and should start pricing a new jersey. Rob holds the Chiefs against Darren, which is lovely, and is backing the Ravens against Steve's Chiefs, which is awkward. Pick a lane, Rob.

Darren is the most likely to spill the coffee. Darren is against the Chiefs in two bets, and the Ravens, Darren's other hope, still can't say whether Lamar Jackson plays Sunday night against Atlanta. Tee Higgins is day-to-day, which by Bengals standards this week counts as good news. Yesterday's advice to watch Falcons tape stands.

Andy, Dan Campbell is changing nothing on a defense that just lost to the Panthers, Rock Ya-Sin is doubtful, and the Lions have slid again to +2400. Loyalty is admirable, but in my opinion it isn't a pass rush. The market gives you 30% in all three of your bets, and I think that's generous.

Lamar Jackson left Sunday's game with an ankle injury, and Jamison Hensley reports he could miss next week's game against the Falcons. Four of the six bets ride on the Ravens, two for Rob and two for Darren, and the man holding all four up just limped off. Trey Hendrickson is out with a finger injury, and Ronnie Stanley and Marlon Humphrey are questionable. Meanwhile the bookies shortened Baltimore's title price from +900 to +850. I can't tell you whether that happened before or after the ankle news, so I won't pretend to. My view is that the Ravens without Lamar are a decent team with a very bad week coming, and Rob and Darren should start watching Falcons tape.

Now for a called shot that blew up. Yesterday this column backed the Raiders' unbeaten run against Mahomes at Allegiant. The Chiefs won 30-27, they're 4-0, and Mahomes still hasn't lost there. Steve, go ahead and gloat. The cost was Tyquan Thornton, who dislocated his ankle and is out. Steve is sitting pretty, and so is Rob on the Kansas City side of things.

Darren, your Bengals lost to Jacksonville. Ja'Marr Chase is questionable with a concussion, Tee Higgins is questionable with a groin injury, and the whole internet has watched Travis Hunter juke Higgins. Cincinnati has drifted out to +1900. Andy, the Lions drifted to +2200 overnight and my notes don't say why. I think that's somehow worse.

Rob, Darren, remember yesterday's confident line about the Ravens' side of the Andy bets looking the healthier one? Baltimore put centre Ethan Pocic and guard Jovaughn Gwyn on injured reserve this morning, and receiver Chris Moore joined Zay Flowers as questionable. That takes two pieces out of the interior of the offensive line in one go, and four of the six bets ride on this team. Oddly, the bookies don't care. Baltimore is an 11.5-point favourite over Tennessee after opening at 8.5, and I can't tell you when the line moved compared with the injury news, so I won't pretend it's connected. My view is that a team that has to work out who its centre is couldn't ask for a gentler opponent than these Titans.

Andy, the Lions and Sam LaPorta have broken off contract talks. Nobody's hurt. Your star tight end just goes into tonight's game at Carolina with his next contract on his mind. Players in that spot either play out of their skin or sulk. I'm calling the first, mostly out of pity.

Steve, the Chiefs have drifted from 5.5-point to 4.5-point favourites at Las Vegas. My read is that the market is pricing in Josh Simmons being out, since he was ruled out mid-week. Mahomes is 6-0 at Allegiant and the Raiders are unbeaten, so something has to give. My money's on the Raiders' unbeaten run. Spare a thought for Rob, who holds the Chiefs against Darren and holds the Ravens against Steve's Chiefs, so he's rooting for Kansas City and against it on the same Sunday.

Andy, the vibes have taken a hit. Brian Branch, the Lions safety, is out with an Achilles injury, and guard Ben Bartch was ruled out this morning too. Cornerback D.J. Reed is questionable with his ribs. Yesterday I called my pick of your Lions over Rob's Ravens shrewd because Carolina had no starting cornerbacks. Today Detroit is missing pieces of its own secondary. The bookies barely blinked and nudged the Lions from 3 to 3.5 points favourites in Carolina. I'm less relaxed. You're the underdog in all three of your bets, and this isn't the week that changes it.

Rob and Darren don't get to gloat for long. Baltimore's top pass rusher, Trey Hendrickson, had surgery on a broken finger and misses Tennessee. Ronnie Stanley is questionable with a toe and Zay Flowers with a hamstring. My hunch is that a finger mends faster than an Achilles, which is why the Ravens' side of the Andy bets still looks the healthier one. But that's a hunch, not a doctor's note.

Steve, the stiff back I mentioned yesterday has turned into a ruling: Josh Simmons is out at Las Vegas. Darren, Kyle Dugger is out and Bryan Cook is questionable, so yesterday's rumour of a secondary is now a vacancy. Meanwhile Rob is the favourite in all three of his bets and is insufferable about it. That's how I'd read his silence, anyway.

Steve, the Chiefs are drifting. The line at Las Vegas opened at 5.5 and now sits at 4.5. In the meantime Kansas City has added offensive tackle Josh Simmons to the injury list with a bad back, and L'Jarius Sneed is still questionable with a knee. My read is that the market noticed the man who protects Mahomes walking stiffly. The Raiders, meanwhile, have started fast enough that people have stopped calling their ground Arrowhead West. A one-point move isn't a crisis, and 3-0 is still 3-0. But Steve has staked three bets on this team without a flicker of doubt, and this is the first week the bookies have shown one.

Rob, you're on Kansas City too, against Darren. Don't laugh at Steve too loudly. Darren, your Bengals have now added cornerback DJ Turner II to that list of questionable safeties, so it isn't so much a secondary as a rumour. Your one comfort is that Burrow has never lost to Trevor Lawrence. I'd want more than that to lean on.

Andy, the Panthers will play Goff without either starting cornerback. That makes my vibes pick of your Lions over Rob's Ravens look shrewder by the day. Rob and Darren can console themselves that Derrick Henry is finally on their side against Tennessee, with Baltimore favoured by 11.5. That is a big number for a team that keeps losing at home.

Rob, Darren: Lamar Jackson is on the injury list with a bad back and is questionable for Sunday. Yesterday this column joked that the bookies had decided Lamar didn't need blockers. This morning the question is whether Lamar needs a heat pad. He has company. Zay Flowers and Marlon Humphrey have hamstrings, Ronnie Stanley has a toe and Trey Hendrickson has a finger, all on top of the two linemen already out. The Ravens have also lost four straight games in Baltimore. The line against Tennessee still reads 11.5, so the bookies are unbothered. I'm bothered on your behalf. Between you, you hold Baltimore in four bets, and that's a lot of eggs in one sore-backed basket.

Andy, this is the best news you've had all season, and you did nothing to earn it. You're at 40% against Darren's Ravens, and my hunch is that number is already out of date. My vibes pick of Lions over Rob's Ravens is starting to look less like spite and more like scouting. Don't get smug, though: Detroit just put centre Cade Mays on injured reserve.

Darren, Cincinnati's casualty list now includes three safeties, Bryan Cook, Jordan Battle and Kyle Dugger, all questionable. The secondary has gone from a problem to a vacancy. Steve, meanwhile, is reading McCourty confess he feels like an idiot for doubting Mahomes. Steve has never doubted anything in his life, which is its own kind of foolishness, but at 3-0 it's working beautifully.

Darren, the Bengals have found the problem, and it was one punt. Ke'Shawn Williams muffed it, the mistake led to Pittsburgh's 30-27 win, and by Tuesday he'd been cut and replaced by Mitch Tinsley. It's decisive, and it misses the point. The same week, cornerback Jalen Davis went on injured reserve with a hamstring, which leaves a secondary that Stephen A. already rates as a problem. Cincinnati are only 2.5-point favourites at home to Jacksonville, which is the market shrugging politely. Rob is 57% in that bet with an unbeaten Chiefs team, and I think that's generous to Darren.

Rob, your week is stranger. Jovaughn Gwyn has joined Ethan Pocic on the out list, so the offensive line is now mostly tape. Yet the Ravens' line against Tennessee has moved from 8.5 to 11.5. Either the bookies think very little of the Titans, or they've decided Lamar doesn't need blockers. I lean toward the second, and so, clearly, does Darren, whose two Baltimore bets suddenly look less like a liability.

Steve, the Chiefs have slipped from 5.5 to 4.5 at Las Vegas, and tackle Josh Simmons went on the list with a bad back. My read is that the two are connected. At 3-0, you'll live. Andy, safety Christian Izien starred for the Lions last week, and they're 3.5-point favourites at Carolina. You're still stuck under 40% in every bet. I'm sticking with yesterday's vibes pick, Lions over Rob's Ravens, mostly because I enjoy watching you both sweat.

Rob, the Rio hangover has arrived, and it's standing where your center used to be. The Ravens lost two centers in that Dallas win. Ethan Pocic is out with a knee, and the plan for Tennessee may be a rookie guard, Vega Ioane, snapping to Lamar Jackson. Add yesterday's Ronnie Stanley toe and that line is held together with tape and hope. Solak is floating Lamar for MVP this morning. I'd settle for Lamar upright on Sunday. Darren, wipe off the smirk: two of your three bets ride on that same wobbly snap.

Andy, your Lions just hung 31 points for a record third straight week to open the season, and they did it while their own center, Cade Mays, went to injured reserve and Ben Bartch was ruled out. The difference is that Detroit seems to score no matter who's standing up front. You're still only 40% in all three bets. I'm starting to think that number is a clerical error, and I'm taking the Lions over Rob's Ravens on vibes alone.

Darren, the Bengals lost B.J. Hill to an Achilles and Colbie Young to a knee, and Stephen A. says the defense is still a problem. When Stephen A. and I agree, it's a bad week. Steve, the juiciest Chiefs-tagged item this morning is Matthew Stafford turning up in a Taylor Swift music video. At 3-0, you can afford to be upstaged.

Rob, you had the kind of Sunday people lie about at barbecues. The Ravens beat Dallas in Rio in the final seconds. Tyler Loop got his redemption, and the Cowboys helped with a late fourth-quarter decision I would love to hear someone defend. Your Chiefs beat Miami 24-10, and Darren's Bengals lost. You're the favourite in all three of your bets, and every one of them went your way. Yesterday I called that Rio pitch a hazard, and Lamar then had one of the big stat days of the week on it. I'll eat that. The only bruise is Ronnie Stanley, now out with a toe injury, and that's Darren's problem too.

Darren, yesterday I said somebody liked your Bengals more than I did. They went to Pittsburgh as 3.5-point favourites, made special teams gaffes, lost a late Burrow fumble and, in the headline's words, couldn't "close it out." I take no pleasure in this. Some pleasure. Your Ravens did carry your other two bets, which is the only reason you're still speaking to Rob.

Steve, I watched that spread slip for two days. Then the Chiefs won by 14, and Mahomes went 14 for 14 on play-action. Consider my eye withdrawn. Andy, Jahmyr Gibbs is getting Barry Sanders comparisons, and you're still the underdog in all three bets. Enjoy the highlight reel.

Andy, your Lions are shopping. ESPN reports Detroit is one of a handful of teams asking the Steelers about cornerback Joey Porter Jr. The news comes with safety Thomas Harper just placed on injured reserve. Nobody has been traded, and asking isn't buying. Still, when a contender starts ringing around for defensive backs in September, I read that as a secondary that knows it's short. Detroit's title price has drifted from +1800 to +2000, and you're the underdog in all three of your bets. It's a shopping trip, Andy, not a rescue.

Rob and Darren, the league has had another look at the Rio grass and says there's "no need to worry." This column called that pitch a hazard, and I'll take the NFL's word when Lamar walks off it in one piece. The market is calmer than I am. This morning Baltimore went from a 3-point to a 3.5-point favourite over Dallas, even with Zay Flowers still questionable. Darren, your Bengals are also in the injury news: receiver Andrei Iosivas is on injured reserve and defensive tackle B.J. Hill is doubtful. Even so, Cincinnati is now a 3.5-point favourite at Pittsburgh after opening at 1.5. Somebody likes your team more than I do.

Steve, yesterday I said half a point wasn't a crisis. This morning the Chiefs slipped another half point, to 9.5 in Miami. It's still not a crisis. But that's two days in a row, and I'm keeping an eye on you.

Rob and Darren, put the coffee down. Ravens tackle Ronnie Stanley has been ruled out with a toe injury, so Baltimore takes Lamar Jackson to Rio without him. The Maracanã pitch is one that NFL and players' union field experts have spent days inspecting. When the union chief has to put out a lengthy statement about the grass, I'd call that a hazard, not a field. Zay Flowers is still questionable with a hamstring. Between you, you hold Baltimore in four bets. You're 60% in the two against Andy and 49% in the two against Steve. If I were you, I'd watch the first series through my fingers.

Andy, don't get smug. Yesterday this column named Ben Bartch as one of four questionable Lions linemen. Today he's out, and safety Thomas Harper is out with him. Detroit is still only a 6.5-point favourite over the Jets, three points less than at the open. Both Ravens-versus-Lions bets now come down to whose offensive line is held together with more tape. I still take Baltimore, on the theory that Lamar can outrun a missing tackle and nobody on your side can.

Steve is the favourite in all three of his bets. The Chiefs' title price has shortened, and Andy Reid gives rookie corner Mansoor Delane a "good chance" of playing in Miami. The line did slip from 10.5 to 10 today. Half a point is not a crisis. Steve's only real problem is that he has nothing to worry about, which is usually when this column starts watching him.

Andy, yesterday this column called Detroit's quiet week a triumph. It lasted a day. Four Lions offensive linemen were listed questionable today: guards Ben Bartch, Christian Mahogany and Tate Ratledge, and tackle Blake Miller. The line against the Jets has slid from Detroit -9.5 at the open to -6.5. I can't tell you when it moved, but my read is that the market saw the same injury report I did. Dan Campbell says he still has faith in defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard. That would be more soothing if Campbell hadn't demoted offensive coordinators mid-season in two of his previous five years. Andy is behind in all three of his bets, and his best chance is 40%. Yesterday Aaron Glenn knew where the weak spots were. Today they have names.

Darren, Cincinnati is heading the other way. The Bengals opened as 1.5-point favourites at Pittsburgh and are now 3.5-point favourites, and their title price has shortened. The biggest drama in Cincinnati is Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins disputing a fine for a celebration. A team whose main complaint is being charged for having fun is a team in a good mood. Rob, your 53% against Darren's Bengals looks generous to me.

Steve, Stephen A. is backing your Chiefs to win the AFC. I'd treat that endorsement like a questionable calf. Rob and Darren, the Rio line has moved toward Baltimore despite the Ravens' injury list. The market is as relaxed as Lamar. I'm not.

Rob and Darren, your Ravens are flying to Rio with a medical ward in the hold. Seven Baltimore players are now questionable: Ronnie Stanley (toe, added today), Trey Hendrickson, Malaki Starks, Chris Moore and three more, on top of the Zay Flowers we already mentioned. Lamar Jackson calls it a business trip and says he isn't worried about the Maracanã pitch. Lovely. The two of you hold Baltimore in four bets, and both of your bets against Steve are sitting at 50%. I'd be less relaxed than Lamar.

Steve, I need to correct yesterday's coronation. I said nothing on the Kansas City injury list explained the market falling for your team. Since then Chris Jones, L'Jarius Sneed and Felix Anudike-Uzomah have all been listed questionable, and today the Miami line slipped from 11.5 back to 10.5. My read is that the market noticed. It isn't a crisis. Kelce leads the league in yards after catch and is running his fastest routes since 2022. You've gone from insufferable to merely smug.

Darren, your quiet good position has sprung a leak. Andrei Iosivas is expected to miss four to six weeks with a thumb injury, and B.J. Hill and Jonathan Allen are both questionable. Rob, that helps your Chiefs bet, the one bet where the Ravens' injuries can't hurt you. Andy, nothing new has gone wrong in Detroit, which by this column's standards is a triumph. Aaron Glenn is coming back to face his old team, though, and I suspect he still remembers where the weak spots are.

Andy, the bookmakers have found a new way to be rude to you. The Lions opened as 9.5-point favourites at home to the Jets and are now 6.5. That's three points gone against the Jets, a team nobody has ever accused of being frightening. The drop lines up with Blake Miller and Christian Mahogany going on the injury list, so my read is that the market doesn't trust what's left in front of the quarterback. In fairness, I told you yesterday those two were out, and the list actually says questionable. Enjoy that correction, because it's the only thing in this column going your way. You're down to 36% against Steve, and I still think all your numbers are flattering you.

Steve, meanwhile, the Chiefs have gone from 7-point favourites in Miami to 11.5, and there's nothing on the Kansas City injury list to explain it. The market has simply decided it likes your team, and you hold them in three bets. Insufferable Steve is back, and fully earned.

Rob, that same move helps your Chiefs bet against Darren, but don't relax. The Bengals have gone from 1.5 to 3.5-point favourites in Pittsburgh and shortened to +1700, and Zac Taylor is out praising Dexter Lawrence. Darren sits at 47% in that bet, which looks like the quietest good position in the pool. And to both Ravens holders: Zay Flowers is listed questionable, which is more than yesterday's column gave him.

Andy, yesterday I said the best day of your week was the one the Lions spent not playing. I'd like to withdraw that as too generous. Avonte Maddox is out for the season with a foot injury. Two offensive linemen, Blake Miller and Christian Mahogany, are listed out. And Dan Campbell spent the day defending his defensive coordinator, Kelvin Sheppard. The reports are already calling this defence "embattled," and when a head coach has to stand up for his DC before Week 3, the defence is the story. The market pushed Detroit out to +2000, the longest price of our four teams. You hold the Lions in three bets and you're the underdog in all three, at 38%, 38% and 37%. My hunch is those numbers are still being polite.

Steve, I owe you a small correction. I said the market wasn't impressed by the Chiefs needing overtime against the Colts. By this morning it had changed its mind and brought them back in to +1200, and the reporting credits Mahomes with using play action to great effect. That's exactly where they were before Sunday, so I'll call it a draw and never mention it again.

Rob and Darren, your Ravens are off to Rio to play the Cowboys, and the NFL says it has "no concerns" about the field. The Ravens say they aren't worried either. With Flowers out, it's nice to hear there's one thing in Baltimore nobody is worried about.

The Ravens were 8.5-point favourites over the Saints yesterday, took a lead into the fourth quarter, and lost. The headline says "another collapse," and the locker room spent the evening declining to compare itself to past Ravens teams, which is what you do when the comparison is obvious. I said yesterday that the bill for that roster arrives in January. I was wrong, because it came in September. Zay Flowers is out, and so are Nnamdi Madubuike (neck) and Teddye Buchanan (ACL). T.J. Tampa is on injured reserve and Ronnie Stanley has a questionable toe. The title price drifted from +900 to +950. Rob and Darren, you hold four Baltimore bets between you, the numbers still favour you in all of them, and I don't believe any of it.

Darren, I asked for the Bengals medicine back on loan. You can have it back, with interest. Cincinnati beat Houston and is 2-0, and the talk this morning is that the defence might be Super Bowl-calibre. The Bengals were the only one of our four teams whose price shortened, from +1800 to +1700. B.J. Hill is out with an Achilles, which is a real loss. Even so, Rob's 52% now looks flattering to Rob.

Steve, the Chiefs beat the Colts 33-30 in overtime. Kenneth Walker III had 178 all-purpose yards and Butker won it from 40. The market's response was to push them out from +1200 to +1300. My read is that it watched a 6-point favourite need overtime and wasn't impressed. Andy, the Lions didn't play and still drifted to +1800. I called it the best day of your week, and I stand by that.

Yesterday I ate my medicine over Joe Burrow's back. This morning the back is on the injury list again: Burrow is questionable for Houston, listed today. The Bengals have also gone from 2.5-point underdogs to 3, and that moved today too. My read is that those two things are connected. The last word we had was a full practice on Friday and a man set to start, and I have nothing saying that has changed, so I won't pretend to know more. But Darren, I handed you that one twenty-four hours ago and I'd like it back, at least on loan. Rob, your 52% still looks stingy to me. I said that once, retracted it, and am now saying it again, which makes me about as reliable as that back.

Steve, something finally happened to you. Chris Jones is questionable with a calf, rookie corner Mansoor Delane is questionable with a shoulder, and the Chiefs slipped from 6.5-point favourites over the Colts to 6 on the day those two were listed. It's half a point, and my hunch is it means nothing. After two days of having no news at all, though, you may find you preferred it that way.

Zay Flowers went from doubtful to out, which surprised nobody who read yesterday's column. Rob and Darren, the Ravens are still 8.5-point favourites and you're still favoured in all four of your Baltimore bets. I still think the bill for that roster arrives in January. Andy, the Lions aren't playing today, so nothing can go wrong for you, and I'd call this the best day of your week.

Zay Flowers is doubtful for Sunday after aggravating that left hamstring and missing most of the week's practices. Nnamdi Madubuike is out with a neck injury, and T.J. Tampa joined the out list this morning with a knee. Trey Hendrickson is now questionable with a finger, of all things. So naturally the Ravens have gone from 7.5-point favourites over New Orleans to 8.5, and their title price has shortened from +920 to +900. My read is that the market is telling you what it thinks of the Saints, not that it missed Flowers limping. Rob and Darren, you share this team across four bets and you're favoured in all four. Enjoy it, but my hunch is that a roster shedding bodies at this rate sends the bill in January. They're wearing all white on Sunday. Matches the bandages.

Now, my medicine. Yesterday I said, loudly, that 52% for Rob over Darren's Bengals looked stingy, and I was leaning on Joe Burrow's questionable back. Burrow then practised in full on Friday and is set to start in Houston. Darren, that one's yours. Rob, I've been shouting on your behalf with no ammunition. Cincinnati is still a 2.5-point underdog and I still prefer the Chiefs, but it's a coin flip and I'll call it one.

Andy, the only Lions news is the title price drifting from +1900 to +2000. No fresh names on the injury list. The market just thought about Detroit a bit longer. Steve, nothing happened to you. Again.

Jack Campbell fought back tears last night and took the blame for Detroit's defense. He's an All-Pro linebacker and he wasn't the one covering all five Josh Allen touchdowns, so I admire the man and fear for the unit. When your best defender is crying at the podium in Week 2, my read is that the problem is bigger than one man's conscience. Andy, you hold this defense in all three of your bets and you're the underdog in every one: 35% against Darren, 42% against Steve, and Rob sitting at 65% against you. The one scrap of comfort is that Avonte Maddox is listed as questionable with that foot rather than anything worse. Blake Miller and Christian Mahogany are both out, though, so the offensive line is thinning now too. My opinion: quietly doomed, and not that quietly.

Steve, the sloth strategy keeps paying. The Chiefs opened as 5.5-point favourites over Indianapolis and the line has grown to 6.5, with Chris Jones's calf still questionable. My read is the market has looked at that calf and shrugged. You've done nothing all week and your price improved. Infuriating.

Rob and Darren, the Ravens' waiting room got two new patients this morning: guard John Simpson (groin) and Ronnie Stanley (toe), both questionable. Baltimore is still laying 7.5 against New Orleans, so nobody's panicking. I'd just like Lamar's bodyguards to be able to walk. Darren, your Bengals are 2.5-point underdogs in Houston with Burrow's back still questionable. I said 52% for Rob looked stingy. I'm saying it louder.

I called the Lions the decoration at someone else's housewarming, and Josh Allen hung them on the wall himself. He scored five touchdowns in a 41-31 Bills win to open the new Highmark Stadium. Compton said beforehand that the Lions' defense was "in trouble", which turned out to be the politest available description. Scoring 31 and losing by ten is a defense that ends bets, Andy, and you hold it in all three of yours. Avonte Maddox left in the second quarter with a foot injury, so the secondary that gave up 41 is now thinner. The market pushed Detroit out from +1900 to +2000. I think that's generous. Andy came in as the underdog against everybody, and my hunch is those numbers are heading south today.

Now, Darren. Yesterday I gave you a rookie with four pressures as the entire Bengals case. Today Joe Burrow is questionable with back tightness, and Compton says that as a Bengals fan he "would be afraid." Cincinnati's next stop is a Texans defense that Will Anderson says just got its "wake-up call." Rob's 52% in that bet looks stingy to me.

Rob and Darren shouldn't get smug about Baltimore. I said the receivers looked like a problem. Ja'Kobi Lane is now on injured reserve and Zay Flowers is questionable with a hamstring. Stanley, Hendrickson and Madubuike are all questionable too. The Ravens drifted from +900 to +920, which is small, but a team with no real problems doesn't carry an injury list that long. Steve, your only worry is Chris Jones's calf, and you're sitting prettiest by doing nothing. That's very on brand.

Andy is the only man in this pool holding the Lions, which means Andy is the only man in this pool with no one to share the blame with. Stephen A. says the defense is a huge concern; I'd go further and say it's the kind of concern that ends bets in October. Pacheco is gone for twelve weeks after back surgery, which leaves Gibbs carrying what the coaches cheerfully call a "big workload" and what I call a countdown clock with hamstrings. And the reward for all this? A primetime trip to Buffalo's shiny new stadium, where the Lions get to be the decoration at someone else's housewarming. Andy, my condolences, respectfully.

Rob and Darren are both sitting on Baltimore against Andy and Steve, which is the smartest thing either of them has done all year, and I suspect entirely by accident. Emmitt Smith is out here admitting Derrick Henry might take his record, and the Ravens' biggest operational decision this week was releasing a kicker because the other kicker was too good. That is a team with no real problems, unless you count the receivers, and the receivers do look like a problem.

Steve's Chiefs beat everyone but Rob and Darren's Ravens on paper — Kenneth Walker looked genuinely good in his debut — though Greeny has already flip-flopped and Stephen A. won't crown them, which is about as close to a warning sign as September offers. Darren also holds the Bengals against Rob. A rookie got four pressures. That's the whole case. Good luck with it, Darren.

Steve is insufferable this week and he has earned it: Kansas City opened with a blowout of Denver, Mahomes back from the torn ACL and Kenneth Walker III looking the part on debut. That's the Chiefs card he holds over Rob, Andy and Darren all at once. Mild comfort for the rest: Stephen A. still won't call Kansas City the team to beat in the AFC, and Greeny has already changed his mind about the Broncos and Chiefs — whatever that's worth in September.

Rob and Darren split the Ravens between them, and Baltimore's news is fiddly rather than dire — Jake Moody cut loose after Tyler Loop's strong opener, and receiver worries with Zay Flowers day-to-day and Ja'Kobi Lane out longer with a wrist.

Andy has Detroit against everybody, so he owns all of it: Isiah Pacheco is out roughly twelve weeks after back surgery, Jahmyr Gibbs is being lined up for a heavy workload, Stephen A. has decided the defense is a concern, and the Lions walk into Buffalo's new stadium in prime time. Darren's Bengals beat, against Rob only, is rookie Howell's four pressures in a win. Quietly the best week of anyone's.
